headline: Apple Mac Studio (M5 Ultra) delivers unlimited power for on-device AI workloads
summary: The M5 Ultra configuration, priced at $11,000, maxes out at 256 GB of unified memory and 80 GPU cores, making it ideal for demanding AI development and high-end video generation.
details: The new Mac Studio with the M5 Ultra chip is positioned as an AI powerhouse, capable of running full agentic AI frameworks and generating high-end video on-device. The top-tier configuration, featuring the M5 Ultra processor and 256 GB of unified memory, is priced at $11,000.

The compact design measures 7 inches square and is about as tall as a coffee mug. Connectivity includes two USB-A ports, four Thunderbolt 5 ports, Ethernet, HDMI, and a headphone jack, supporting up to four 5K external displays at 120 Hz. It also features a front-facing SD card slot, beneficial for photographers and videographers.

A more accessible M5 Max model starts at $2,499, offering 36 GB of memory and 512 GB of storage. This configuration provides similar performance to the M5 Max MacBook Pro but at a substantially lower price, with more expandability options for storage and memory.

The M5 Ultra is Apple's most powerful chip to date, a quad-die design that stitches together two M5 Max chips. It boasts a total of 36 CPU cores and up to 80 GPU cores, delivering unprecedented performance for highly targeted professional workflows.

Each GPU core across the entire M5 family now includes a Neural Accelerator, significantly enhancing AI workload performance. This dedicated hardware ensures improved efficiency and speed for machine learning tasks directly on the device.

Benchmarking reveals the M5 Ultra Mac Studio outperforms the M5 Max by 51% in Cinebench 2026 for CPU performance. GPU performance also sees a significant boost, being 32% faster than the M5 Max, making it ideal for demanding gaming and AI applications.

headline_marked: Russian missile strikes [[take out popular piracy websites]]
headline: Russian missile strikes take out popular piracy websites
summary: Russian missile strikes have targeted Ukrainian data centers, causing "Direct Destruction of Server" attacks. This led to explosion-induced downtime for popular torrent sites 1337x and NordicQuality.
details: The Russo-Ukrainian war has extended into the digital realm, with Russian military forces reportedly targeting Ukrainian data centers. This has resulted in what some are calling "Direct Destruction of Server" attacks, a physical form of digital disruption.

Popular torrent trackers 1337x (Leet X) and NordicQuality experienced explosion-induced downtime. 1337x, which typically sees 40-50 million monthly visits, and NordicQuality were temporarily brought offline by kinetic blasts hitting their network infrastructure.

Multiple Ukrainian data center firms were affected. Virtual Systems reported strikes that temporarily took down its facilities, MiroHost Ukraine was completely destroyed, and CosmoNova, DataGroup, and CityHost also sustained hits. Telco KyivStar's headquarters in Kyiv were also struck.

Despite these physical attacks, both 1337x and NordicQuality have since come back online. This incident underscores the evolving nature of warfare, where physical attacks on digital infrastructure can have far-reaching consequences for internet services globally.
